review.en: A serious writer in 1960s Hong Kong grinds out martial-arts and sex serials for money and drinks to bear it. Liu Yichang tells it in fragmented first person, often called the first stream-of-consciousness novel in Chinese, with one chapter only a line long. Its portrait of a literary conscience worn down by the market is bitter, funny and still recognisable.
review.zh: 六十年代香港，一个有理想的作家为了糊口，替报馆写武侠和色情连载，靠酒撑下去。刘以鬯用破碎的第一人称写成，常被称为中国第一部意识流小说，有一章短到只有一行。文学良知被市场磨损的样子，写得苦涩、好笑，今天读来仍不陌生。
